speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome. I see you are presenting with increasing yellow discoloration of the eyes and skin. To better understand your condition, can you tell me if your baby was born prematurely or if there were any complications during the delivery?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-week-old female newborn. The patient has been experiencing increasing yellow discoloration of her eyes and skin for 2 days. She was born at 39 weeks' gestation, initially weighed 3066 g and now weighs 3200 g. The patient is exclusively breastfed.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. Since the jaundice is appearing at 2 days of age and is increasing, have you noticed any feeding difficulties or signs of dehydration? Also, has your baby had any stool color changes, such as clay-colored stools?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Increasing yellow discoloration of the eyes and skin. I also have Exclusively breastfed, Brother died 3 months after liver surgery.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Breast Milk Jaundice. While the family history of a sibling with liver disease requires monitoring, the clinical presentation of worsening jaundice in a well-appearing, exclusively breastfed 2-week-old without signs of dehydration or pale stools is most consistent with physiological breast milk jaundice. I recommend checking Total Serum Bilirubin and Direct Bilirubin levels to rule out hemolysis or biliary obstruction.
